title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) as a candidate marker associated with venous thromboembolism risk factors in sepsis: an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis affects over 19 million people worldwide annually and is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which significantly worsens clinical outcomes. However, current biomarkers such as D-dimer lack specificity, and the molecular signatures associated with VTE risk in sepsis remain unclear. METHODS: We applied integrative transcriptomics and machine learning approaches to identify VTE-associated biomarkers in sepsis-related datasets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential gene expression analysis, and immune infiltration assessments were conducted using publicly available datasets. Candidate biomarkers were further evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, Cox regression, nomogram modeling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) validation. RESULTS: p BATF BATF p BATF Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) emerged as a top candidate biomarker, significantly associated with both sepsis and VTE-related datasets (fold change >1.5,< 0.001).expression showed consistent elevation across multiple independent cohorts and demonstrated discriminatory performance for disease- or risk-score-defined phenotypes, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.831 to 0.953. Highexpression was associated with prolonged prothrombin time and 28-day mortality in sepsis patients (= 0.024). Single-cell analysis showedenrichment in macrophages and dendritic cells. CONCLUSION: BATF may serve as a candidate biomarker associated with high VTE risk phenotypes and 28-day mortality in sepsis-related cohorts. However, BATF was not validated against adjudicated or imaging-confirmed VTE events in this study; therefore, it should not be interpreted as a diagnostic marker for confirmed VTE or a direct predictor of thrombosis. Prospective cohorts with adjudicated VTE outcomes are required to confirm its clinical utility.

title: An Entropic Value-at-Risk-Inspired Load-Balancing Routing Algorithm for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) space-air-ground integrated networks, risk-neutral reinforcement-learning-based routing methods for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks remain susceptible to severe tail latency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel Entropic Value-at-Risk (EVaR)-inspired routing algorithm with risk regularization for low-return actions. The routing process in an LEO satellite network is formulated as an event-driven partially observable Markov decision process. Within a multi-agent soft actor-critic framework, an EVaR-inspired state-level risk proxy for low-return actions is introduced and incorporated into the actor loss as a risk regularizer. This design enables the joint optimization of expected routing returns and the mitigation of low-return action risk. Simulation results obtained in a simplified LEO network using Iridium orbital parameters demonstrate that, compared with the multi-agent soft actor-critic algorithm, the proposed algorithm reduces the average end-to-end delay and the 99th-percentile end-to-end delay by 19.2% and 32.9%, respectively. It also reduces the average and maximum queueing delays by 79.4% and 57.0%, respectively, with approximately no packet loss observed during the simulations. These results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enables efficient and reliable routing in LEO satellite networks under high-load conditions.

title: Coenzyme Q10 for Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection: Protocol for a Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Feasibility Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency. Emergency surgery is the standard life-saving treatment, but some patients decline operative repair, and no established pharmacological therapy has been shown to stabilize acute TAAD. Preclinical work by our team implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching in aortic dissection and suggests that coenzyme Q10 may reduce dissection-related injury. This study aims to determine the feasibility of a future definitive randomized trial and to obtain preliminary safety and exploratory efficacy information.This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center feasibility trial will enroll 60 adults with CTA-confirmed Stanford type A aortic dissection within 24 h of symptom onset who decline emergency surgical repair after standard surgical counseling. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to oral coenzyme Q10 100 mg three times daily or matched placebo for 14 days, in addition to the same guideline-directed supportive medical care. The primary feasibility outcome is recruitment feasibility, defined as randomization of 60 participants within 12 months after recruitment initiation. Secondary feasibility outcomes include treatment adherence, follow-up completion, dropout, missingness, outcome-assessment feasibility, and candidate endpoint event rates. The primary exploratory clinical outcome is 14-day all-cause mortality; additional exploratory outcomes include aortic rupture death, false-lumen thrombosis, cardiac tamponade, worsening pericardial effusion, and organ malperfusion syndromes. Safety outcomes include adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse drug reactions, suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, and prespecified laboratory indices.The trial is designed to establish whether recruitment, blinded treatment delivery, follow-up, outcome collection, and safety monitoring are operationally feasible and to provide estimates for planning a larger confirmatory trial.This feasibility trial will inform the design and conduct of future definitive evaluation of coenzyme Q10 in acute TAAD. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600123230.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification.This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples.POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation.This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

title: Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment. A revision-stage locked five-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS-only model serving as the comparator. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples. RESULTS: Post-hoc Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 (23.8%) had END48. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.651 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.601 (0.511 to 0.723). The corrected AUC difference vs. the NIHSS-only model was 0.038 (-0.025 to 0.171). The corrected Brier score was 0.180, compared to a prevalence-only reference of 0.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0.9%. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0.731 (0.519 to 0.892). Incremental net benefit was -0.015, 0.036, and 0.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero.Riley assessments across plausible model-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation. CONCLUSION: Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required.

title: The snake-head sign on MRI in craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas: a novel imaging feature and a hypothesis of venous remodeling and congestion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Craniocervical junction (CCJ)-region dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs) are rare but potentially reversible causes of venous congestive myelopathy, often difficult to recognize due to non-specific presentation. We observed a characteristic pattern of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on sagittal MRI, involving the medulla and upper cervical cord with a rostral end divided into ventral and dorsal limbs, which we termed the "snake-head sign." This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of this feature among reported CCJ-region dAVF cases and explore its clinical and anatomical correlates. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed published cases of CCJ-region or adjacent dAVFs reported between 1996 and 2026 that included retrievable sagittal T2-weighted or FLAIR images. The presence of the snake-head sign was assessed, and clinical, angiographic, and treatment-related variables were extracted, including fistula location, feeding artery, draining vein direction, treatment modality, and outcome. Associations with the sign were evaluated using univariate analyses. Given the retrospective, literature-based design and limited sample size, findings were considered hypothesis-generating. RESULTS: Among 64 reported cases, the snake-head sign was identified in 31 (48.4%). No significant associations were found between the sign and age, sex, symptom duration, feeding artery, treatment modality, or outcome. However, a non-significant trend was observed for venous drainage configuration: cases with cranial convergence of the draining vein toward the CCJ more frequently demonstrated the sign, whereas purely caudal drainage patterns showed it less often. Fistulas at lower cervical nerve-root sleeves, requiring a longer cranial venous course, also showed higher sign frequency. These findings suggest the sign may reflect venous outflow geometry rather than arterial source or fistula location. CONCLUSION: The snake-head sign is a recognizable MRI feature present in roughly half of reported CCJ-region dAVF cases. Its identification may raise clinical suspicion for CCJ-related dAVF, particularly in unexplained venous congestive myelopathy. The trend toward a higher frequency of the sign in cases with cranially convergent venous drainage raises the hypothesis that it reflects concentrated venous congestion at this anatomical transition zone. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized imaging review and angiographic correlation are needed to confirm its diagnostic value and clarify the underlying mechanism.

title: Anxiety in patients with lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis: a patient-centred sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of prevalence, associated factors, and patient experiences.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (LEDVT) is associated with substantial psychological burden. Anxiety after DVT may reflect not only an emotional consequence of thrombosis, but also a signal of unmet informational, functional, and supportive care needs. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with anxiety among LEDVT patients and to explore their lived experiences, perceived triggers, and support needs using a mixed-methods design. METHODS: A sequential explanatory mixed-methods study was conducted. In the quantitative phase, 175 LEDVT patients completed the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (B-IPQ), and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS). Clinical and care-process variables were collected, including the perceived adequacy of structured counselling at diagnosis using an 8-item checklist. Clinically significant anxiety was defined as GAD-7 score ≥10. Multivariable logistic regression was performed according to a prespecified conceptual framework. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 purposively selected participants; data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: P P P P The prevalence of clinically significant anxiety was 41.1% (72/175; 95% CI: 33.9%-48.6%). Younger age (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98, = 0.002), higher B-IPQ score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.11-1.26, < 0.001), lower MSPSS score (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98, = 0.005), and adequate counselling at diagnosis (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.20-0.88, = 0.022) were independently associated with anxiety. Qualitative analysis generated five major themes: fear of complications, treatment-related anxiety, role and functional impairment, information delivery and illness meaning-making, and insufficient emotional and social support. CONCLUSION: Anxiety affects approximately two in five LEDVT patients in this single-centre cross-sectional cohort. Anxiety was associated not only with younger age, negative illness perception, and low social support, but also with symptom burden and perceived inadequacy of counselling at diagnosis; qualitative findings additionally highlighted symptom burden and functional limitations as key experiential drivers of anxiety. Integrated DVT care should address anticoagulation management, structured education, risk communication, cognitive reframing, functional recovery, and psychosocial support.

title: Risk factors of major bleeding associated with direct oral anticoagulant treatment in patients with venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are commonly prescribed for venous thromboembolism (VTE), but major bleeding (MB) remains an important complication of treatment. Despite their widespread use, systematic evaluations of prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE. This study seeks to enhance the safety and efficacy of anticoagulation therapy for VTE patients. METHOD AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to search the PubMed and Web of Science databases for studies published before September 18, 2026. The review adhered to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to identify studies that investigated risk factors for major bleeding associated with DOAC treatment in patients diagnosed with VTE. Among the evaluated prognostic factors, quantitative pooling was possible only for age, which was reported in two studies; the remaining factors were summarized individually. Low-certainty evidence from a single study suggested a possible association between non-recommended dosing regimens and major bleeding. Evidence regarding declining adherence was also limited and of very low certainty. For age, very low-certainty evidence from the pooled analysis of two studies did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with major bleeding. CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests possible associations between several prognostic factors and major bleeding in patients with VTE treated with DOACs; however, most findings are supported by low- or very low-certainty evidence and frequently by single studies. These findings should therefore be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, high-quality prospective studies.

To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE.

title: Case Report: Brucella-associated complications following thoracic endovascular aortic repair: a case series of three patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection. Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. Case presentation: We report three elderly male patients who developed severe aortic complications following TEVAR, including pseudoaneurysm formation and aorto-esophageal fistula. All patients had a history of epidemiological exposure to Brucella and were diagnosed with active infection through serological testing (Rose Bengal test, serum agglutination test, Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies). Endovascular re-intervention combined with targeted anti-brucellosis therapy was performed in all cases. RESULTS: One patient achieved sustained clinical remission after repeat endovascular repair and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Two patients developed catastrophic infectious complications, including mediastinal abscess and aorto-esophageal fistula, resulting in death despite aggressive management. CONCLUSIONS: Brucella infection should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained symptoms after TEVAR, especially in endemic regions. Endovascular repair plays a critical role in acute stabilization; however, long-term outcomes remain highly dependent on effective infection control.

title: Anatomical distribution of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism: a retrospective study with finite-element analysis of calf muscle-vein mechanics.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Muscular calf vein thrombosis is frequently detected by whole-leg ultrasonography, but its relationship with pulmonary embolism (PE) and the mechanical response of the intramuscular veins during calf-muscle contraction remain incompletely defined. We examined PE prevalence across anatomical categories of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and used a structural finite-element model to quantify contraction-related venous compression and identify the regions in which deformation was greatest. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients evaluated for a first episode of lower-extremity DVT between May and October 2022. DVT was classified as isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis, isolated axial calf DVT, isolated proximal DVT, or combined muscular calf and proximal DVT. PE was diagnosed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography or pulmonary perfusion imaging. Because several cells contained few observations, the four-group distribution was compared using a Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. A separate finite-element analysis used one normal computed tomography angiography geometry. Gastrocnemius contraction, soleus contraction, and co-contraction were modeled as structural loading conditions. Spatial stress and strain maps were examined to localize venous regions with the greatest structural response. No blood-flow, venous-valve, or thrombus model was included. RESULTS: p 3 Among 160 patients with DVT, 30 had PE. PE was present in 14 of 125 patients with isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis [11.2%, exact 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.3%-18.1%], 1 of 4 with isolated axial calf DVT (25.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-80.6%), 3 of 10 with isolated proximal DVT (30.0%, 95% CI: 6.7%-65.2%), and 12 of 21 with combined muscular calf and proximal DVT (57.1%, 95% CI: 34.0%-78.2%). The overall distribution differed across groups (exact < 0.001). At the final recorded model-loading parameter, mean muscle von Mises stress was 21.51 kPa during gastrocnemius contraction, 1.16 kPa during soleus contraction, and 9.68 kPa during co-contraction. The corresponding changes in modeled venous-domain volume were -49.25, -17.07, and -64.08 mm, respectively. The spatial maps showed nonuniform venous deformation, with the most prominent response concentrated around proximal branching regions and adjacent intramuscular venous segments. CONCLUSIONS: PE prevalence differed across the anatomical DVT categories and was highest when muscular calf and proximal veins were involved concurrently. The structural model provided direct evidence that calf-muscle contraction compresses deep veins and localized the regions of greatest deformation. These findings support targeted dynamic venous imaging, while effects on blood flow and thrombus behavior require prospective patient-specific validation.

title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RESULTS: P P P RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. CONCLUSION: Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with lung cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with lung cancer are at high risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet their awareness and preventive behaviors remain insufficiently characterized. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among patients with lung cancer and explored factors associated with these dimensions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 patients with lung cancer recruited at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between January and May 2026. Participants completed a KAP questionnaire regarding VTE prevention. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with KAP outcomes, and Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the associations among knowledge, attitudes, and practices. RESULTS: The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 8.98 ± 3.52, 31.18 ± 3.37, and 19.19 ± 4.49, respectively. Rural or suburban residence (adjusted OR = 0.447, 95% CI 0.201-0.992) and no previous VTE education (adjusted OR = 0.271, 95% CI 0.147-0.501) were associated with lower odds of meeting the operational knowledge threshold. Higher knowledge scores were associated with more favorable attitudes and higher self-reported preventive practice scores, while higher attitude scores were associated with higher self-reported preventive practice scores. CONCLUSION: Patients with lung cancer showed persistent gaps in VTE-related knowledge, generally favorable responses to several attitude items, and heterogeneous self-reported preventive behaviors. The findings highlight potential targets for patient education, particularly among rural or suburban residents and those without previous VTE education.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. METHODS: n n In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( = 409) and a validation cohort ( = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. CONCLUSION: The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty. RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control. CONCLUSION: Systematic Review Registration: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. In contrast, NOAC use, surgical interventions, high BMI, statin and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, and early rhythm-control strategies were linked to reduced mortality risk.https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024533372, PROSPERO CRD42024533372.

title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets.In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test.Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00;< 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00;< 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm;< 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (= 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test,< 0.001).In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559). CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

title: Case Report: Endovascular repair for true lumen collapse after frozen elephant trunk for type A aortic dissection.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) was applied in the treatment of type A aortic dissection, enabling one-stage repair of the aortic arch and proximal descending aorta while promoting true lumen expansion. However, inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen is a rare but catastrophic complication that may cause true lumen collapse and life-threatening visceral malperfusion, with limited reports on its endovascular management. CASE PRESENTATION: Here, we present the case of a 44-year-old female who underwent Bentall procedure, total arch replacement, and FET implantation for acute type A aortic dissection at a local hospital. Postoperatively, she developed visceral malperfusion manifesting as abdominal distension, hepatic and renal dysfunction, and elevated lactate levels. Computed tomography angiography revealed that the FET stent had been inadvertently deployed into the false lumen, resulting in true lumen collapse. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed, establishing a "FET-false lumen-true lumen" pathway with an additional stent graft to redirect aortic flow into the true lumen. Computational fluid dynamics analysis showed that the postoperative hemodynamics have been significantly improved. The patient's organ function normalized, and she was discharged two weeks later, remaining asymptomatic at 8-month follow-up. CONCLUSION: Endovascular reintervention with additional stent grafting to establish a flow-redirection pathway is a feasible and effective strategy for true lumen collapse following inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen. Prompt recognition, timely imaging confirmation, and immediate intervention are paramount to mitigating the risks associated with this serious complication.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.

title: Redox Dysregulation in the Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Wall: Ferroptosis and Experimental Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a spatially heterogeneous disease of the aortic wall for which no pharmacological treatment has reliably arrested enlargement. The term oxidative stress encompasses processes that differ in chemical form, anatomical location and cellular effect. This narrative review examines haem and redox-active iron, phospholipid peroxidation and antioxidant defence at the intraluminal thrombus-wall interface and within medial and inflammatory cells. We distinguish ferroptosis from redox effects on coagulation, migration and secretion and relate these functions to wall remodelling. Experimental studies show that manipulating iron uptake and ferritin turnover, membrane phospholipid susceptibility or peroxide detoxification can alter vascular smooth muscle cell survival, macrophage behaviour and aortic injury. The cellular function affected helps determine which process an intervention should preserve or suppress. Based on evidence from human tissue and animal models, we review opportunities to localise, manipulate and monitor these processes and assess their relevance to established AAA. Testing after confirmation of aneurysm formation, with target engagement in defined wall cells and parallel assessment of systemic effects, is needed to determine whether these approaches can limit continued enlargement.

title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain. METHODS: n n This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, = 87; TAV, = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up. RESULTS: P P No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion. CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited. METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12. DISCUSSION: Clinical Trial Registration: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population.

title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79;= 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66;= 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15;= 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02;= 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98;= 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (for interaction = 0.64). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

title: The Central Coupler of ClpXP Controls Intersubunit Communication and Couples Intrasubunit Chemical Energy with Force Generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management.

title: Dickkopf-3 (DKK3) in cardiovascular diseases: from a stress-responsive biomarker to a potential therapeutic target.
abstract: Dickkopf-3 (DKK3) is a secreted glycoprotein that functions as a context-dependent modulator of the Wnt/β-catenin and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling pathways. Originally studied in development and cancer, DKK3 has recently emerged as a key stress-responsive factor. It is released by epithelial and other cell types under pathological strain and actively participates in fibrotic, inflammatory, and remodeling processes across various organ systems. In cardiovascular medicine, DKK3 is gaining recognition not only as a promising biomarker for renal and vascular injury-conditions closely intertwined with cardiovascular outcomes-but also as a direct mediator in the pathogenesis of specific cardiovascular conditions such as abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and heart failure. This review synthesizes current knowledge on DKK3, beginning with its fundamental biology and established roles in renal, pulmonary, and dermal fibrosis, which provide crucial mechanistic parallels. We then focus on the evolving evidence of DKK3's involvement in cardiovascular diseases, critically evaluating its biomarker potential for risk stratification in conditions like diabetic kidney disease and its direct pathophysiological roles in vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype switching, myocardial remodeling, and aneurysm formation. We delve into specific molecular mechanisms, including interactions with the ATF6-TGFβ3-Smad2/3 axis and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1), as revealed by preclinical models. Finally, we explore the therapeutic implications of targeting the DKK3 axis, discuss the challenges posed by its context-dependent dual roles, and outline future research directions necessary to translate these discoveries into clinical applications for cardiovascular patients.

title: Vascular aging biomarkers: the role of ADMA, SDMA, and inflammation.
abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment based on traditional risk factors may not fully capture subclinical vascular injury and vascular aging, supporting interest in biomarkers reflecting underlying vascular mechanisms. Endothelial dysfunction, altered methylarginine metabolism, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent interconnected processes that may contribute to vascular aging. This narrative review summarizes evidence on the associations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, symmetric dimethylarginine, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with subclinical atherosclerosis and vascular aging. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched between January and August 2026, with priority given to studies evaluating associations of these biomarkers with subclinical vascular changes, vascular aging, and cardiovascular outcomes. ADMA shows the most consistent associations with subclinical atherosclerosis, although these vary across arterial territories and vascular measures. Evidence for SDMA in early vascular disease is more limited, and interpretation is complicated by its dependence on renal function, although some associations persist after adjustment for renal function. IL-6 has biological and genetic evidence supporting a role in atherogenesis, but its associations with subclinical atherosclerosis are not consistently independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. hsCRP is an established cardiovascular risk marker and has also been associated with progression of carotid stenosis and arterial stiffness. Differences in vascular endpoints, study populations, confounder adjustment, and analytical methods contribute to heterogeneity across studies. Overall, these biomarkers appear to reflect partly distinct but interconnected components of vascular aging. Their potential relevance may lie in their complementarity; however, current evidence does not establish that combined assessment improves evaluation beyond conventional approaches. Prospective studies should determine whether their combined assessment improves identification of accelerated vascular aging beyond conventional risk assessment.

title: Case Report: Fatal recurrent rupture of multiple pancreatic pseudoaneurysms following acute alcoholic pancreatitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic pseudoaneurysm (PPA) is a severe and life-threatening vascular complication of pancreatitis. This case highlights the critical need for comprehensive vascular assessment and surveillance in patients with alcoholic pancreatitis to prevent fatal adverse outcomes. CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old man with a 30-year history of heavy alcohol intake (500 mL of 52% ABV Baijiu daily, corresponding to an estimated 205 g pure ethanol per day) presented to our emergency department with hematemesis and hemorrhagic shock on 2 April 2026. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis complicated by a pancreatic pseudocyst at another hospital in November 2025 but did not receive standardized follow-up and treatment. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed rupture of a pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm with hemorrhage extending into the duodenum. Emergency transarterial embolization of the gastroduodenal artery was performed, and hematemesis resolved temporarily. Subsequently, the patient developed progressive abdominal pain, distension, and peritoneal irritation signs. Repeat CT confirmed recurrent intra-abdominal hemorrhage. A second digital subtraction angiography (DSA) identified an unrecognized feeding branch arising from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) supplying the pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully embolized. The patient's condition stabilized temporarily, with a gradual increase in hemoglobin levels. On 14 April 2026, the patient suffered sudden severe abdominal pain and abdominal distension. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT revealed enlargement and rupture of a pre-existing tiny pseudoaneurysm in the splenic hilum, resulting in massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage. The patient developed refractory hemorrhagic shock followed by cardiac arrest during preparation for emergency endovascular intervention and ultimately died. Post-embolization hemodynamic changes may have contributed to progressive enlargement and subsequent rupture of the pre-existing lesion, although this causal mechanism cannot be definitively proven in this single case. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysms may be multifocal. Successful control of a dominant bleeding lesion does not eliminate the risk of rupture of the separate pre-existing small pseudoaneurysm, and incomplete initial angiography limited only to the celiac trunk may miss SMA feeding branches, even after technically successful initial endovascular intervention for pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysm.

title: Drug-coated balloon, drug-eluting stent, versus bare-metal stent for vertebral artery ostial stenosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stenosis at the origin of the vertebral artery (VAOS) accounts for approximately one in five posterior circulation ischemic events. Bare-metal stents (BMS) have been the conventional endovascular treatment, but restenosis occurs in 11-67% of cases. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stents (DES) are alternative strategies; however, no network meta-analysis has compared all three modalities specifically at the vertebral origin. METHODS: Five databases-PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, and Wanfang-were searched from 2010 through May 2026 for studies comparing at least two of DCB, DES, or BMS in adults with symptomatic VAOS. The search identified 499 records; 393 underwent title and abstract screening after deduplication, from which 60 full-text articles were assessed. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted using the netmeta package (R 4.5.2), with Bayesian sensitivity analysis. The primary endpoint was imaging-confirmed restenosis (≥50%). The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261413981). RESULTS: N I I 2 2 Seven studies (three randomized trials and four observational cohorts, = 970; range 46-217) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with BMS, both DES (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.17-0.45) and DCB (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.83) reduced restenosis. DES and DCB did not differ significantly from each other (OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.58-3.50). Between-study heterogeneity was modest (= 20.5%). Although the point estimate suggests modest heterogeneity, the wide confidence interval and the small number of studies limit precision. Lowin a small network should not be equated with clinical homogeneity. P-scores ranked DES first (88.9%), DCB second (60.7%), and BMS last (0.4%). For perioperative safety, DCB ranked highest (P-score 90.0%). CONCLUSION: Both DES and DCB reduce restenosis compared with BMS in VAOS. Both DES and DCB are associated with lower restenosis rates than BMS. The relative anti-restenosis efficacy of DES versus DCB remains uncertain due to the absence of direct head-to-head comparisons. Treatment selection should be individualized based on lesion characteristics and procedural considerations. The DCB evidence base remains small, and head-to-head comparisons of DES versus DCB at the vertebral origin are needed. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261413981, Identifier: CRD420261413981.

title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

title: Dual-guidewire technique with cerebral embolic protection for brachiocephalic trunk bifurcation stenosis: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery is a rare and highly challenging lesion of the supra-aortic vessels. Endovascular intervention carries a high risk of embolization and difficulty in delivering large-diameter stents. CASE SUMMARY: We report a 60-year-old male patient who presented with intermittent dizziness and asymmetric blood pressure in the upper limbs. Color Doppler ultrasound and head and neck CT angiography revealed severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk (stenosis rate approximately 90%), with the lesion involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery, accompanied by right subclavian artery steal phenomenon. The patient underwent brachiocephalic trunk balloon angioplasty and stenting via a single femoral artery access. An embolic protection device was deployed in the C1 segment of the right internal carotid artery for distal cerebral protection. During delivery of the stent, the filter guidewire provided insufficient support; a second guidewire was added as a buddy wire to establish a dual-guidewire rail technique, facilitating successful stent placement. Debris was observed in the retrieved filter. Postoperatively, the severe stenosis was relieved and the steal phenomenon resolved. At 1.5 years of follow-up, the patient reported no recurrence of dizziness, and the inter-arm blood pressure difference remained within the normal range. CONCLUSION: In this selected case with clear antegrade flow direction, a single-access, single-filter strategy appeared feasible and may offer a simplified alternative for similar anatomical presentations. However, further validation in larger case series is warranted. The application of dual-guidewire rail technique to overcome difficulties in large-diameter stent delivery during brachiocephalic trunk intervention has been rarely reported.
